A content delivery network, or CDN, is a system of computers spread around the world that work together to deliver websites and videos quickly, no matter where a visitor happens to be located. Without one, every request for a webpage would travel all the way back to a single origin server, the original computer where the website's files are permanently stored. That trip can be slow if the visitor is far from that server. A CDN solves this by copying popular files onto many smaller computers positioned closer to visitors; each of these nearby computers is called an edge location, sitting at the "edge" of the network, nearer to homes and offices than the origin server does. Think of it like a chain of bakeries: instead of everyone driving to one central bakery across the country for bread, smaller branches near each neighborhood keep fresh loaves on hand, so people are served quickly from nearby. When a visitor requests a page and the nearby edge location already has a saved copy ready to hand over, that's called a cache hit, and the page loads almost instantly because nothing had to travel far. If the file is not yet stored there, the edge location fetches it once from the origin server, saves a copy, and delivers it to future visitors just as fast. This constant copying and reusing is why streaming video rarely buffers and websites feel fast around the globe.

| Term | Plain meaning | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| Origin server | The main computer where a website's files live permanently | It is the ultimate source of truth whenever no nearby copy exists |
| Edge location | A smaller computer placed close to visitors, holding copies of popular files | It shortens the distance data has to travel, making pages load faster |
| Cache hit | When a nearby edge location already has the requested file ready | It means near-instant delivery with no long trip back to the origin server |
| Cache miss | When the nearby edge location does not yet have the file | It causes a short delay while the file is fetched once and then stored for next time |
